source_locator: Auditor report to Council dated December 5, 2012, Mayor table, Total column
verification_note: The City Auditor certified abstract for the November 6, 2012 Portland nonpartisan election lists Mayor totals across Multnomah, Clackamas and Washington counties: Charlie Hales 163,522 (61.18 percent), Jefferson Smith 83,741 (31.33 percent), write-ins 20,039. The scanned report and the City results page agree on these totals. No primary candidate had a majority on May 15, 2012 (Hales and Smith advanced), so the November election between the top two is the decisive round. The official name for the stage is the general election; it was the runoff between the two primary nominees.

source_locator: Amended Report to Council dated July 6, 2016, Mayor table, Total column
verification_note: The City Auditor amended certification (July 6, 2016, adding eight Clackamas ballots) lists Mayor totals across three counties: Ted Wheeler 105,975 (54.71 percent), Jules Bailey 32,041 (16.54 percent), Sarah Iannarone 22,857. Wheeler holds a majority of the mayoral vote and the report states he is elected under City Code Section 2.08.040, so the scheduled November runoff was not held. The Multnomah County results summary shows the same totals. The earlier June 15, 2016 certification had Wheeler at 105,973, which the amendment corrected to 105,975.

source_locator: Auditor report to Council dated December 2, 2020, Mayor table, Total column
verification_note: The City Auditor certified results for November 3, 2020 state that two candidates appeared on the ballot for a run-off election for Mayor. Ted Wheeler received 167,260 votes (46.07 percent) and Sarah Iannarone 147,964 (40.76 percent), with 47,832 write-in votes, across three counties. Wheeler had 49 percent on May 19, 2020, short of a majority, so the November round decided the office. The Multnomah County summary shows the same totals.

source_locator: Multnomah County final tabulation JSON for City of Portland Mayor, round 20 tally
verification_note: Portland elected its Mayor by ranked-choice voting on November 5, 2024. The county final tabulation (contest file dated 2024-11-29) gives round 20 totals: Keith Wilson 153,522 and Carmen Rubio 106,431, with a threshold of 129,977. The City Auditor report to Council certifies Keith Wilson as elected with a final-round share of 59.06 percent against 40.94 percent for Rubio, which matches these counts. Vote totals are final-round totals of continuing ballots, not first-choice totals.
